- Piece\
One piece of work handed over: its prompt, with each question settled in it, and the tools it
may use.
- Worktree\
The folder and the branch where a piece works, apart from the person's own and from each other
piece's.
- Conversation\
The talk with the model in which a piece works. It goes on after each reset with all the piece
has done.
- Record\
Where a piece stands, its waits, and its last words, for any later session to read.
- Wait\
One stretch in which the usage limit held a piece, from its stop to the reset.

more.good_when: The developers read from each row alone when its check runs and how they tell that it passed: no row names one time in its When and another in its criterion, as the walkthrough run's row does, and no criterion asks them to break each part by hand on each change to see a case fail, as the traceability row does.

Two developers who build how the next piece gets its number decide it the same way from the document, so that on the person's second night, with the first night's branches, worktrees, and records kept or some of them removed, each new piece gets a folder and a branch that no earlier piece holds, and its record's folder name agrees with that number.
